CHME 2310 — Transport Processes 1 | prerequisites, offerings, professors (Northeastern)

NU Map is an independent, student-built planner — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data comes from the public catalog on a schedule; confirm with the official catalog and an advisor.

4 semester hoursUndergraduateLectureusually offered: fall, springtypical days: W/ThBostonTraditional

Covers the fundamentals of transport of incompressible and compressible fluids (fluid flow) along with energy transport. Concepts are continued in CHME 3312 with emphasis on heat transport. The methods taught are relevant to the analysis of engineering processes in a number of industries, including chemical, pharmaceutical, food, energy, biotechnology, and materials.

Prerequisites

(MATH 2321 (min D-) and CHME 2308 (min D-) and MATH 2341 (min D-))
